title: Revithada
subtitle: Slow-baked Greek chickpeas with lemon and rosemary
excerpt: Dried chickpeas soaked overnight and then baked slowly in a clay pot with olive oil, rosemary and lemon. A dish from Sifnos island where the pot goes into the oven for hours.
sourceNotes: Sifnos island tradition, Greece. Historically baked in the village bread oven overnight.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions with the cooking liquid. Defrost overnight and reheat gently.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well in a larger casserole. Allow extra baking time for a bigger batch.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Improves the next day. Reheat in the oven at 160C covered, or on the hob with a splash of water.

content.text: Revithada needs time. The chickpeas soak overnight, then bake for three hours until they are creamy inside and the liquid turns to a light broth. Start the soak the evening before.

items.prepNote: soaked overnight in cold water, drained

content.text: The evening before: soak the dried chickpeas in a large bowl of cold water. They will double in size. Drain before using.
Heat the oven to 180C. Put the drained chickpeas into the dutch oven.
Add the onion, garlic, rosemary sprigs and lemon slices. Pour over the olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Pour in the hot water. The liquid should cover the chickpeas by 2cm. Add more if needed.
Cover tightly with a lid or foil. Bake for 2 hours.
Remove the lid and bake for a further 45 minutes. The broth will reduce and darken slightly.
Taste the broth and adjust the salt. Serve in deep bowls with crusty bread.

items.symptom: The chickpeas are still hard after 3 hours.
items.cause: The chickpeas were not soaked long enough, or the water was too hard.
items.fix: Return to the oven with more hot water and continue baking. Old dried chickpeas can take up to 4 hours.

items.cause: The lid was not sealed tightly and too much steam escaped.
items.fix: Add 200ml of hot water and cover tightly. Check every 30 minutes from now on.

items.cause: Salt was not added before baking.
items.fix: Season generously now and stir. The chickpeas will absorb salt slowly over a further 15 minutes.
